ru.shadow_mine: Ха! Вылитая я! Посмотрим, умеешь ли ты вкалывать, как я.
ru.shadow_other: Не знаю, на кого ты пашешь, но не давай себя загонять.

voice_notes: Winona is a blue-collar factory handywoman: clipped, folksy speech with dropped g's ('workin''), 'ain't', 'outta', 'hey?' tags and a pleased 'Ha!', and she sees everything through work ethic, shifts, overtime, worker solidarity and the right tool for the job, while treating "magic" and nightmare fuel with plain suspicion ('I don't trust that thing one bit.', 'Too lazy to do your own chores, Max?', 'Workers gotta look out for one another.'). PT carries her with colloquial 'tá', 'pra', 'né?', 'Eita' and labour idioms ('Já bati o cartão!', 'Bem que a gente pode botar as sombras pra trabalhar.'). ZH keeps her blunt and spoken, with 哈！, 是吧 for 'hey?', 这玩意儿/东西 for suspect objects and workplace vocabulary (加班费, 工伤赔偿, 上工: '不妨让暗影们也上上工。', '我信不过那东西。'). RU uses rough colloquial Russian ('штуковина', 'фиговина', 'сдох', 'халтурит', 'смена') with 'а?' for 'hey?' and inverted emphatic order modelled on 'Не доверяю я этой штуке.' and 'Чертов пульт сдох.'

line_notes.codex: Calls back to her vanilla Codex line but lets her pragmatism win: she still distrusts magic, yet she'd never turn down a useful tool.
line_notes.codex_needsfuel: Uses her stock 'outta juice' phrasing for dead machines plus her established distrust of nightmare fuel, so it clearly says the book needs refuelling.
line_notes.no_max_sanity: Frames the shadows as her work crew (like 'I'm not lookin' to expand my workforce') and the strain as a pounding head, so it plainly reads as 'can't summon more'.
line_notes.shadow_mine: Facing a copy of herself, the proud worker immediately sizes up whether it matches her own work ethic.
line_notes.shadow_other: Her worker-solidarity streak ('Workers gotta look out for one another.') aimed at a stranger's shadow labourer whose boss she doesn't know.
